# Citations

All sources used in the OpenAPI-Driven Type-Safe Frontend Development research.
Numbered sequentially. Each entry includes the specific data extracted and a
source quality tier.

---

**[1]** "openapi-fetch." *openapi-ts.dev*, n.d.
<https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-fetch/>
**Tier:** 2
Bundle size (6 KB minified), 300k ops/s GET benchmark, architecture as
type-safe wrapper around native Fetch API, data/error/response return
structure, platform support (Node 18+, TS 4.7+), path-based client variant
limitations.

**[2]** "openapi-react-query." *openapi-ts.dev*, n.d.
<https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-react-query/>
**Tier:** 2
1 KB wrapper around @tanstack/react-query, available hooks (useQuery,
useMutation, useSuspenseQuery, useInfiniteQuery, queryOptions), setup pattern,
type safety guarantees.

**[3]** "Hey API — OpenAPI to TypeScript." *heyapi.dev*, n.d.
<https://heyapi.dev/>
**Tier:** 2
Plugin ecosystem (8 validation, 4 state management, 6 mocking, 10+ web
frameworks), supported HTTP clients (Fetch, Axios, Ky, Angular, Next.js, Nuxt,
OFetch), notable users (Vercel, OpenCode, PayPal), MIT license.

**[4]** "SDK Plugin." *heyapi.dev*, n.d.
<https://heyapi.dev/openapi-ts/plugins/sdk>
**Tier:** 2
Tree-shaking support (flat/function-based default is tree-shakeable,
class-based is not), generation approaches (flat vs single strategy),
configuration options (auth, validation, nesting).

**[5]** "Migrating from openapi-typescript-codegen." *heyapi.dev*, n.d.
<https://heyapi.dev/openapi-ts/migrating>
**Tier:** 2
File structure changes (models.ts → types.gen.ts, services.ts →
services.gen.ts), any → unknown type change, removed/renamed options
(useUnionTypes, indent, useDateType), service generation now functions by
default (tree-shakeable).

**[6]** "Orval." *orval.dev*, n.d.
<https://orval.dev/>
**Tier:** 2
v8 current version, generates type-safe API clients, framework-native hooks
(React Query, Vue Query, Svelte Query, Solid Query, SWR, Angular), HTTP
clients (Fetch, Axios), mock generation (MSW, Faker.js), Zod integration.

**[7]** Nottingham, M.; Wilde, E.; Dalal, S. "Problem Details for HTTP APIs."
*RFC 9457*, IETF, July 2023.
<https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9457>
**Tier:** 1
Five core fields (type, status, title, detail, instance — all optional),
media types (application/problem+json, application/problem+xml), changes from
RFC 7807 (IANA registry, multiple problems guidance, tag URI scheme), extension
naming rules, forward compatibility (clients MUST ignore unrecognized
extensions).

**[8]** "Problem Details: Getting API Errors Right with RFC 9457."
*Redocly Blog*, n.d.
<https://redocly.com/blog/problem-details-9457>
**Tier:** 3
RFC 7807 vs 9457 differences summarized as "small but mighty": multiple
problems representation, shared IANA problem type registry, clearer field
associations. RFC 7807 remains viable; immediate migration unnecessary.

**[9]** "Problem Details (RFC 9457): Doing API Errors Well."
*Swagger Blog*, n.d.
<https://swagger.io/blog/problem-details-rfc9457-doing-api-errors-well/>
**Tier:** 3
Extension usage recommended over parsing detail property. Example with code
field, errors array, pointer references ("/name").

**[10]** "Middleware & Auth." *openapi-ts.dev*, n.d.
<https://openapi-ts.dev/openapi-fetch/middleware-auth>
**Tier:** 2
Three callbacks (onRequest, onResponse, onError), callback ordering (request
in order, response in reverse), onError handles only network/CORS errors (NOT
4xx/5xx), early response pattern, conditional middleware via schemaPath,
client.use/eject lifecycle, stateful body handling caveat.

**[11]** "Examples." *openapi-ts.dev*, n.d.
<https://openapi-ts.dev/examples>
**Tier:** 2
Runtime validation via openapi-ts-router with Zod/Valibot, three error
handling approaches (axios-style throws, fetch-style tuple, safe/all-catching),
"A good fetch wrapper should never use generics," mockResponses() testing
helper.

**[12]** "Migration Guide — openapi-typescript." *openapi-ts.dev*, n.d.
<https://openapi-ts.dev/migration-guide>
**Tier:** 2
v7.x breaking changes: TypeScript AST instead of string transformations,
--default-non-nullable on by default, globbing replaced with
redocly.config.yaml explicit schemas, file paths must use URL objects,
strings now support inline YAML/JSON.

**[13]** "API Versioning." *Speakeasy*, n.d.
<https://www.speakeasy.com/api-design/versioning>
**Tier:** 3
Change taxonomy (additive vs breaking), URL versioning, media-type versioning,
evolution strategy, Sunset header with Link header, OpenAPI 3.1+ deprecated
keyword. Cost formula: "If it's two days of work, and there are 10 customers,
that's 160 person-hours."

**[14]** "API Versioning Best Practices." *Redocly Blog*, n.d.
<https://redocly.com/blog/api-versioning-best-practices>
**Tier:** 3
Evolution vs explicit vs hybrid (recommended) versioning. Deprecation
timeline: 6-month announcement, 12 months migration support, 18-24 months
total. Stripe hybrid example. Track endpoint usage before removal.

**[15]** "API Versioning." *Stripe Engineering Blog*, n.d.
<https://stripe.com/blog/api-versioning>
**Tier:** 3
Rolling date-based versions (e.g., 2017-05-25), account auto-pinning, version
change modules, nearly 100 backward-incompatible upgrades over six years, API
review process. Response processing: format current → determine target version
→ walk backward applying version modules.

**[16]** "oasdiff." *oasdiff.com*, n.d.
<https://www.oasdiff.com/>
**Tier:** 3
300+ categories of breaking changes, OpenAPI 3.0 fully supported / 3.1 beta,
GitHub Action (PR annotations, automated comments, approval workflows), CLI
(oasdiff breaking, oasdiff changelog), web tool (browser-based, not stored).

**[17]** "OpenAPI Spec Drift Detection." *Speakeasy Blog*, n.d.
<https://www.speakeasy.com/blog/openapi-spec-drift-detection>
**Tier:** 3
Drift defined as "traffic not present in your schema served by your API."
Speakeasy SDK checks API traffic against uploaded schema. Webhook-based
notifications.

**[18]** Hatfield, T. et al. "Schemathesis." *schemathesis.io*, n.d.
<https://schemathesis.io/>
**Tier:** 2
Property-based testing from API schemas, finds server crashes / schema
violations / validation bypasses / stateful bugs, 5-15 issues on initial
production runs, supports OpenAPI 2.0/3.0/3.1 and GraphQL, CI via GitHub
Actions (schemathesis/action@v2), ICSE 2022: 1.4x-4.5x more defects than
other tools.

**[28]** "Internal Packages." *Turborepo Documentation*, n.d.

**Tier:** 2
JIT packages (export TS directly, no build step, consumer bundler transpiles,

**[29]** "Nullable Handling in OpenAPI." *Speakeasy*, n.d.
<https://www.speakeasy.com/openapi/schemas/null>
**Tier:** 3
OpenAPI 3.0.x: nullable:true. OpenAPI 3.1: type: ['null', 'string'] or oneOf
with type: 'null'. Three-state problem (present/null/omitted). "SDK generators
need special wrapper types to express all three states." Best practice: only
combine optional + nullable when null and omitted produce different outcomes.

**[30]** "oneOf, allOf, anyOf: OpenAPI Tips." *Speakeasy Blog*, n.d.
<https://www.speakeasy.com/blog/openapi-tips-oneof-allof-anyof>
**Tier:** 3
oneOf → TypeScript union, allOf → intersection, anyOf → no standard mapping.
anyOf causes "combinatorial explosion" (200+ types from 5 inputs). Speakeasy
interprets anyOf as oneOf. Best practice: avoid anyOf unless necessary.

**[31]** "Issue #1520: Empty object in allOf creates Record<string, never>."
*GitHub (openapi-ts/openapi-typescript)*, 2023.
<https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript/issues/1520>
**Tier:** 4
Empty object in allOf generates Record<string, never>, making intersection
impossible to satisfy. Workaround: --empty-objects-unknown flag. Maintainer
acknowledged "no reason a person would want Record<string, never> as part of
an intersection." Issue remains open.

**[32]** "Circular References." *pb33f libopenapi documentation*, n.d.
<https://pb33f.io/libopenapi/circular-references/>
**Tier:** 3
Automatic detection via model building (non-destructive). Infinite loops
determined by required field status. Configuration flags:
IgnorePolymorphicCircularReferences, IgnoreArrayCircularReferences. Result
metadata: IsPolymorphicResult, IsArrayResult, IsInfiniteLoop. Best practice:
distinguish benign circles from infinite loops.

**[33]** "belgif/openapi-problem." *GitHub*, n.d.

OpenAPI data types compliant with RFC 9457. Within a major version, types
remain backwards compatible once released. Referenced by Belgif REST guide for
